transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m just… really exhausted. My body feels drained. Even walking in from the car or opening the EHR at work feels like it takes everything I’ve got.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or motivation in things you usually enjoy, or do you just feel physically tired?
Mostly physical, I think. My body just feels completely drained… like even walking from my car or opening the EHR takes everything I’ve got.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or motivation in things you usually enjoy, even when you're not physically tired?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that. It feels more like I’m just too wiped out to do anything.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time lately?
Yeah… most days, I guess. Since my energy dropped, I’ve just felt kind of empty. Hopeless, too… like I already messed up my future in healthcare before it even really started.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to that… I just know I’m too tired to do much, so it’s hard to tell.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you still get enjoyment out of things you used to like, like hobbies or spending time with friends?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really tested that. Most of the time I just feel too drained, so I don’t know if I’d enjoy it or not.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, no longer feel satisfying or pleasurable to you?
I don’t really know. I guess I haven’t paid enough attention to whether it’s “not pleasurable” or if I’m just… not doing much right now.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore—even when you’re not physically tired?
I still don’t really know. I haven’t noticed it that clearly… I mostly just haven’t been doing those things.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or being with friends, feel less rewarding or enjoyable than they used to be?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying attention to it like that… I just haven’t really been doing much of those things lately.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, feel less enjoyable or rewarding than before?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been doing them enough to tell, I guess.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, feel less enjoyable or rewarding than they used to be?
I guess I can’t really say. I haven’t been doing those things enough lately to know if they feel different.

I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying attention to whether it feels “rewarding” or not… I just haven’t been doing much of that stuff.
Even when you’re not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy — like hobbies or spending time with friends — feel less enjoyable or rewarding than they used to be?
I’m not really sure. I know you’re asking that, but… I haven’t been doing much with friends or hobbies lately, so I can’t tell if it’s less enjoyable or just not happening.
Even when you’re not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy — like hobbies or spending time with friends — feel less enjoyable or rewarding than they used to be?
I don’t think I can answer that clearly. I haven’t really been doing those things enough to know if they feel different.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy — like hobbies or spending time with friends — feel less enjoyable or rewarding than they used to be?
I guess I still don’t really know. I haven’t been doing much of that stuff, so… it’s hard to say if it feels less enjoyable or if I’m just not trying.
Even when you're not physically tired, do you find that activities you used to enjoy — like hobbies or spending time with friends — feel less enjoyable or rewarding than they used to be?
I don’t really know how else to answer it. I haven’t been doing much of those things lately, so I can’t tell if they feel less rewarding or if I’m just… not getting around to them.

I’ve kind of already said it… I’m not sure. I haven’t really been around friends or doing hobbies enough lately to know if it feels less enjoyable.
